cold_open: Six more division games. Kevin Swanson carries a 193-win lead into them, Fadi sits one win from 175, and the two managers who set the best and worst lineups of Week 1 have drawn each other.

notes.Shawn|Thomas: Thirty-eight meetings and Shawn is two up, but Tom has taken three of the last five. Both opened with a loss — Shawn managing 96.5 percent of his roster, Tom scoring 69.18 against an 85.49 projection.
notes.Brian Clark|Eric: Eric has won four of the last five in a series barely six games old, and opened with both the quarterback and the receiver of the week. Clark spent Week 1 ending a three-game skid against Tom.
notes.Evan|Steve Swanson: Evan leads 16–14 and has won four of the last five, including the last by 21. Steve opened by beating his projection 35.62, more than anyone; Evan by winning the week's biggest blowout.
notes.Douglas|Fadi: Fadi's lead has never been bigger, and Doug lost the last one by 2.79. Week 1 pushed them further apart: Fadi set the best lineup in the league, Doug the worst — and the lowest score.
notes.Jeff|Kevin O'Boyle: O'Boyle leads 8–5, but their last meeting was the lowest-scoring in the series, 63.37–58.90. Jeff opens off the league's best score; O'Boyle off 38.04 points left on his bench.
notes.Dominic|Kevin Swanson: Dominic has won four of the last five, the last of them the highest-scoring meeting these two have ever played. Swanson took Week 1 with the ninth-best score; Dominic lost with the third-best.

milestone.label: Kevin Swanson · Career Wins
milestone.text: Kevin Swanson opens Week 2 with 193 career wins, two clear of Brian Clark. Fadi is one win from 175 of his own, and 30.75 points from 27,500 for his career. Consolation games don't count. They never did.

history_lines.text: Thomas goes big in week two

kicker: All six are division games again, as they were in Week 1 and will be in Week 3. The cross-division schedule starts in Week 4.
